newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Plutonic says hard to beat '96 profit.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Plutonic says hard to beat '96 profit.

text.p: Gold miner Plutonic Resources Ltd said on Tuesday that it would be hard to beat its calender 1996 earnings result.

"We said last year it would be substantial challenge to better the previous year's profit and we are saying the same thing this year," managing director Ron Hawkes told reporters after the annual meeting.
Hawkes also said the company expected to exceed last year's gold production of 450,000 ounces.
"The real challenge for us in 1997 is the level of costs that we achieve," Hawkes said.
Cash costs this year would be between A$350 and A$400 an ounce compared with about A$400 last year.
Hawkes said the company did not expect to reach its full production level until the year 2000.
The Centenary mine would commence operations later this year and would take 2.5-3 years to reach production. Centenary is next to Plutonic's Darlot underground mine in Western Australia.
A plant to treat ore from the new mine would cost between A$80-A$100 million but a prefeasibility study was yet to be conducted, Hawkes said.
Plutonic, which is 31.8 percent owned by Malaysia Mining Corp Bhd, achieved a net profit of A$40.70 million in calendar 1996 from A$40.12 million in 1995.
Pre-tax operating profit fell to A$37.69 million from A$43.68 million in 1995.
